Concept Description: Biological sex of the participant as recorded by the study. BDC-HM slot: Demography.sex (SexEnum: MALE, FEMALE, UNKNOWN). Use when the variable records the participant's own sex, including variables labelled 'gender' that record male/female (BDC-HM has no gender-identity slot). Not for the sex of a relative or of a child. The CURIE is the V1 reference code for the concept (verified in OMOP/Athena); BDC-HM does not emit a concept code for Demography, the slot itself carries the meaning.
Example source variable description: Sex [Visit 7/NCS Derived Variable Dataset. DERIVE71]|GENDER|Reported gender|SEX OF PARTICIPANT|Gender (F=Female, M=Male)|Participant Sex|Gender|EXAM 1 SEX, TELEPHONE INTERVIEW|Medical History - Female Reproductive History: Male Participant (if male skip to Smoking Questionnaire/MD07)

Concept Description: Self-identified race in the U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB) categories. BDC-HM slot: Demography.race (RaceEnum; multivalued). Use for a race item, a check-all-that-apply race block, or a combined race/ethnicity variable. A Hispanic/Latino answer is Ethnicity, not Race. Not for genetic ancestry estimates (principal components, admixture proportions). The CURIE is the V1 reference code for the concept (verified in OMOP/Athena); BDC-HM does not emit a concept code for Demography, the slot itself carries the meaning.
Example source variable description: Race [Visit 7/NCS Derived Variable Dataset. DERIVE71]|RACE|Race|Racial or ethnic group|Cumulative race|WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BEST DESCRIBES YOU? (CHECK ALL THAT APPLY): CAUCASIAN OR WHITE|SPECIFY OTHER RACE|Black, African-American, or Negro

Concept Description: Hispanic or Latino origin in the OMB two-category scheme (Hispanic or Latino / Not Hispanic or Latino), regardless of race. BDC-HM slot: Demography.ethnicity (EthnicityEnum). Use for a Hispanic/Latino yes/no item, a Hispanic subgroup item (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Dominican, Central or South American), or the Hispanic code of a combined race/ethnicity variable. Not for country of birth or language alone. The CURIE is the V1 reference code for the concept (verified in OMOP/Athena); BDC-HM does not emit a concept code for Demography, the slot itself carries the meaning.
